pages.text: A reaction goes at the rate constant k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT): hotter is faster, and the higher its activation energy Eₐ, the more heat it needs. In a stirred vessel a batch held for a residence time τ reaches the conversion X = 1 − e^(−kτ). Each recipe needs its own conversion; a shorter τ runs more batches. A catalyst lowers Eₐ - but sinters if run too hot.
$(thing)Set$(): Heater temperature, Residence time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Heater drift: the temperature the reaction sees varies by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The vessel is over its rated temperature; The catalyst is sintering: it wears ten times as fast.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Batches follow the residence time: 60 s is the normal pace.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Rate constant: k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$(br)Conversion: X = 1 − e^(−kτ)$(br)Time to the target: t = −ln(1 − X_target)/k
